summary: Frontend-only WebXR park app tested end-to-end via Playwright on the public preview URL. Welcome screen, park scene rendering (trees, bench, path, sky, particles), initial HUD prompt, pointer lock + WASD HUD switch, W movement to bench + sit prompt + crosshair active state, E key sit/stand toggle (both directions), ambient audio toggle click and exit button all work correctly. Only one critical defect found: clicking the VR button produces an UNCAUGHT pageerror ('not connected to three.js. You either might be missing the <XR> component or the canvas is not yet loaded?'). All other acceptance criteria pass.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking the 'Entra in VR' button in a browser without an XR device triggers an UNCAUGHT pageerror: 'not connected to three.js. You either might be missing the <XR> component or the canvas is not yet loaded?'. The requirement states the VR button must degrade gracefully with no uncaught runtime errors. Root cause: `xrStore.enterVR()` is called inside `setTimeout(..., 150)` in Home.jsx AFTER `setMode('vr')`, but ParkExperience is lazy-loaded via Suspense so the <XR> Canvas often isn't mounted yet at t=150ms. Additionally, `enterVR()` returns a Promise whose rejection is NOT caught (the try/catch only wraps the synchronous call).

action_items: Fix VR button uncaught error in /app/frontend/src/pages/Home.jsx. Two-part fix recommended: (1) wait for ParkExperience/Canvas to be mounted before calling `xrStore.enterVR()` (e.g., pass an `autoEnter` prop to ParkExperience that calls enterVR from a useEffect once the XR provider is mounted, or use a ref/callback set by ParkExperience). (2) Handle the promise rejection: `xrStore.enterVR()?.catch((e) => console.warn('VR not available:', e))` so the async rejection is not uncaught. This should eliminate the 'not connected to three.js' pageerror.
critical_code_review_comments: Home.jsx: The try/catch around `xrStore.enterVR()` does not catch the Promise rejection. Chain `.catch()` on the returned promise.

Home.jsx: Racing the lazy import with a fixed 150ms setTimeout is fragile. Prefer coordinating VR entry with the actual mount of the <XR store={xrStore}> element (e.g., via effect inside ParkExperience when mode==='vr').
ParkExperience.jsx: The keydown listener for 'E' is registered on window; consider capturing behavior when other inputs are focused (not currently an issue but noteworthy).

DesktopPlayer.jsx: The canvas click handler treats ANY canvas click within 2.9m of bench as a sit intent AND raycasts screen-center against the bench even when not pointer-locked. This can cause the very first pointer-lock-acquisition click (which is intentionally aimed at canvas center in the docs/tests) to inadvertently trigger sit mode if the bench happens to be in the screen center. Consider requiring pointer lock to already be active before raycasting for sit.
SitController.jsx: The useEffect dep list intentionally omits `bench`, `mode`, `camera` (with eslint-disable) — safe today but flag for future refactors.

success_rate.frontend: 95% (10/11 features passing; only VR-button graceful-degradation fails)

context_for_next_testing_agent: App URL: https://322a02a1-9f13-4254-9c03-f5cb01797288.preview.emergentagent.com/. Frontend-only WebXR + Three.js. Use viewport 1920x800. IMPORTANT: To reach the bench via W, click canvas at (200, 100) (sky corner) to acquire pointer lock WITHOUT the first click's raycast/near-bench check triggering sit mode (clicking at (960,400) can hit the bench and instantly toggle sit). Then keyboard.down('KeyW') + wait 2000ms + keyboard.up('KeyW'). After that: sit-prompt appears, crosshair gets .active class, and E toggles sit<->stand correctly. To exit reliably in headless, call `await page.evaluate('() => document.exitPointerLock()')` before clicking [data-testid=exit-park-button] with force=True — keyboard Escape does NOT release pointer lock in headless Chromium (this is a Playwright/headless quirk, NOT an app bug — real browsers release lock on Escape natively). All HUD data-testids confirmed working: welcome-screen, enter-vr-button, enter-desktop-button, welcome-step-01/02/03, park-experience, click-to-play-prompt, desktop-hud-controls, sit-prompt, stand-prompt, ambient-audio-toggle, exit-park-button.
verified_flows: Welcome screen: Italian hero 'Cammina nel parco respira il silenzio' + VR/Desktop buttons + 3 steps (Muoviti/Guarda/Siediti) all present
Desktop button transitions to park-experience with WebGL canvas
Park scene renders trees (green), wooden bench, grass ground, sky, beige path, particles — no black screen, no missing-texture console errors
Initial HUD 'Clicca per attivare mouse e tastiera' visible; after canvas click pointer lock engaged and desktop-hud-controls (WASD hint) visible
Holding W ~2s moves camera; sit-prompt appears; crosshair gains .active class
Pressing E toggles sit: stand-prompt appears, sit-prompt hides; pressing E again toggles back
exit-park-button (top-right, 'Torna all'ingresso') returns to welcome-screen when pointer lock is released

rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: Load /. Click [data-testid=enter-vr-button]. Within ~2s, an uncaught error surfaces in the browser (Playwright captures it via 'pageerror' event, and React dev overlay shows a redbox).
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: In /app/frontend/src/pages/Home.jsx, enterVR() sets mode='vr' (which triggers a lazy-loaded ParkExperience via Suspense) and then, after a fixed 150ms setTimeout, calls xrStore.enterVR(). Two issues: (a) 150ms is not enough for the async chunk import + Canvas mount, so the XR provider isn't yet connected to the three.js renderer when enterVR() runs; (b) enterVR() throws asynchronously (returned/rejected Promise) — the try/catch around the sync call misses this rejection, so it becomes an unhandled promise rejection surfaced as a pageerror.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: 1) Attach `.catch()` to the promise: `xrStore.enterVR()?.catch(err => console.warn('VR not available:', err));`. 2) Instead of a 150ms setTimeout race, trigger VR entry from inside ParkExperience via a useEffect that runs once XR is mounted (e.g., pass an `autoEnterVR` prop and call xrStore.enterVR() in an effect there).
rca_of_the_issue.impact: Users on non-XR devices see a red error overlay in dev builds; in production the promise rejection is silently swallowed by the browser (still logged). The app remains functional otherwise (user can still click exit and return to welcome).
